ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The main body in the figure is a 74161 synchronous 4-bit binary counter, with output terminals Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4 at the top. On the right side there is a gate circuit labeled “&”, whose input lines select Q1, Q2, Q4 from the output terminals and introduce them, used for decoding; the output of this gate is connected to the synchronous load terminal \overline{LD} of the 74161. The lower D1, D2, D3, D4 load input terminals are all connected to low level, that is, the preset data is 0000. The clear terminal remains inactive, and the count enable terminal is connected into the count-enabled state. Reasoning: According to the problem meaning, the 74161 counts upward, and Q1 is regarded as the least significant bit and Q4 as the most significant bit. The decoding condition is Q4=1, Q2=1, Q1=1, and Q3 does not participate in decoding. When the count starts from 0000 and counts upward, the first state satisfying Q4=1, Q2=1, Q1=1 is Q4Q3Q2Q1=1011₂, that is decimal 11. In this state, the decoding signal causes the active-low synchronous load terminal \overline{LD} to be triggered; therefore the next clock edge will not continue to 1100, but will synchronously load D1-D4=0000. Thus the cyclic states are decimal 0 to 11, a total of 12 states, so this circuit is a modulo-12 counter.
